audit.why: Rumble 48.56% over 1775 games. Jayce owns levels 1-5 on range, Rumble gets leverage at 6 and wins the two-item war of attrition — the chart already says exactly that and matches the win rate.
Four spikes at 1-3, 6, first item and 2+ items are correctly placed. Only the mechanics attached to the level-6 spike needed fixing.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says Acceleration Gate lets him 'reliably land Shock Blast through minion bodies'.
audit.why: Riot's description: Shock Blast 'detonates upon hitting an enemy'. Minions detonate it. The gate raises missile speed, range and damage — it does not make the orb pass through the wave. The page even contradicts itself, since wants.you[0] correctly tells you to keep minion bodies in the way.
audit.corrected: Stand behind the wave; the orb pops on the first minion it touches.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stance swap is never given a cooldown, and the armour/MR shred on his cannon-form first attack is never mentioned.
audit.why: Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer is a 6-second swap and it is an auto-attack reset; the first attack in cannon form reduces your Armour and Magic Resist. Against a Rumble that is the tell that the burst rotation has started — and it is 6 seconds, not free, so he cannot swap out of a bad spot on demand.
audit.corrected: Name the 6s swap and the shred as the burst tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two places describe Flamespitter as something he interrupts — 'Flamespitter never gets a clean channel', 'before you can channel Flamespitter back'.
audit.why: Flamespitter is not a channel; it burns in a cone for 3 seconds and keeps burning through knockback. Thundering Blow's real cost is that it moves YOU out of the cone, so the burn lands on empty ground.
audit.corrected: Reframed around cone position, not interruption.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Shock Blast's cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 and 6s at rank 6 — the single number that decides when a Rumble is allowed to walk forward.

edits.before: The acceleration gate at level 2 turns Shock Blast into a skill-shot he can reliably land through minion bodies; your Heat management means nothing if you are losing 15% HP per wave.
edits.after: Acceleration Gate makes Shock Blast faster, longer and harder, but the orb still detonates on the first minion it touches — hold the back of the wave and his level-2 pattern stalls.

edits.before: Full cannon kit online — gate-Q, E knockback in hammer form, and free stance-swap mean Jayce controls the distance at every moment, and Flamespitter never gets a clean channel.
edits.after: Gate-Q, Thundering Blow in hammer form and a 6-second stance swap mean Jayce owns the distance — the knockback does not stop Flamespitter, it just moves you so the cone burns air.

edits.before: The Equalizer is your first real leverage — a line cast across the wave-path forces him off the cannon stance he needs, opening a trade window on its cooldown.
edits.after: The Equalizer is your first real leverage — burn the ground he pokes from and he must walk out of it, and a 6-second stance swap will not reposition him for free.

edits.before: Track Shock Blast's cooldown and commit your Flamespitter walk-up only in that window, double-E-slow him before he can hop back to cannon
edits.after: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 and 6s maxed — walk up only in that gap, then double-harpoon him before he swaps back to cannon

edits.before: Bait your Scrap Shield with a cannon poke, then all-in with hammer form while your shield is on cooldown
edits.after: Swap to cannon so the first attack shreds your MR, then poke a Rumble whose Scrap Shield is already down

edits.before: At Level 6 the dynamic shifts in one specific way: Equalizer. If you land it across his path when he tries to cannon-poke you or zone the wave, he eats the full burn and cannot swap stances inside it cleanly. That threat alone makes him respect distance, which finally puts bodies between his Shock Blast and your face. However, his Eclipse first item spike is genuinely dangerous — one gate-Q into hammer E knockback clears your shield and deletes a third of your HP before you can channel Flamespitter back. Track his cannon Q cooldown religiously, and use Equalizer to open trades rather than to confirm kills you cannot execute at this HP threshold.
edits.after: At Level 6 the dynamic shifts in one specific way: The Equalizer. Land it across the ground he pokes from and he has to walk, and the stance swap is a 6-second cooldown, not an escape button. That threat alone makes him respect distance, which finally puts minion bodies between Shock Blast and your face — the orb detonates on the first one it touches. His first-item spike is still genuinely dangerous: gate-Q into Thundering Blow clears your shield and knocks you clean out of your own cone, so the burn finishes on empty ground. Track Shock Blast, 16s at rank 1, and open trades with R rather than trying to confirm a kill you cannot execute.

edits.before: Two items in, Liandry burn plus Shadowflame makes your Equalizer a fight-ending tool and your sustained Danger Zone Flamespitter wins the extended damage war against a Jayce who cannot freely kite through a burning rocket-line. The 1v1 is still skill-dependent — he can burst through your shield with a clean combo — but teamfights are yours if you place the Equalizer across the choke before he can pick a safe stance. Never Equalizer into open air hoping he walks into it; place it where he must be, not where he is.
edits.after: Two items in, Liandry burn plus Shadowflame makes The Equalizer a fight-ending tool and sustained Danger Zone Flamespitter wins the extended damage war against a Jayce who cannot freely kite through a burning rocket-line. The 1v1 is still skill-dependent — a clean gate-Q into cannon shred bursts through your shield — but teamfights are yours if you place the wall across the choke before he can pick a safe stance. Never fire The Equalizer into open air hoping he walks in; place it where he must be, not where he is.

notes: The page contradicted itself on the matchup's core spacing rule: whys[1] said Acceleration Gate lets Shock Blast pass through minions, while wants.you[0] correctly said to keep minions in the way. Riot's text is explicit that the orb detonates on the first enemy hit, so the wave really is the answer. Added the two missing numbers that make the advice actionable — Shock Blast 16s/6s and the 6-second stance swap — plus the armour/MR shred on his cannon-form first attack as the burst tell. Also removed two 'channel Flamespitter' phrasings: Flamespitter is not interruptible, Thundering Blow simply relocates you out of the cone.
